result.summary: Encloses all non-comment header contents within `#ifndef`/`#endif` include guards and adjusts Doxygen file-level comment formatting across multiple headers. Updates `test/lint/lint-include-guards.py` to flag any non-empty, non-`//` lines located outside include guards.
result.problem: Several headers place includes, code, or namespace closures outside their include guards, preventing compilers from applying once-only header optimizations. Additionally, several headers had improper Doxygen `@file` formatting, and existing lint checks did not prevent content from slipping outside include guards.
evidence: PR description cites GCC documentation on once-only header optimization: 'From https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/cpp/Once-Only-Headers.html'
result.scope_notes: Combines include guard structural fixes with Doxygen comment refactoring across 15 header files and an update to the python include-guard linter.
result.changed_since_previous: Added Doxygen file-level documentation cleanups across several header files (converting block comments to `//` lines and standardizing `@file` / `@brief` usage) to satisfy the stricter linter rules.
result.card: Encloses all header content within include guards and updates test/lint/lint-include-guards.py to enforce that no non-comment lines exist outside header guards. Also standardizes Doxygen file comment formatting across multiple headers so they pass the linter. This enables compiler once-only header optimization and prevents future guard regressions. The change is based on PR 36815 and is a prerequisite for PR 36808.

risk.why: Only rearranges include guards, header comment formatting, and linter checks with no functional logic changes.
